chapter_theme: The placing of grace (திருவருள் வைப்பு): grace is what binds the soul and what frees it, the whole course of a life from birth to dissolution, and the five acts by which the Lord makes and pervades the worlds. The Lord cannot be reached by one's own knowing; he enters the heart of those he graces, and is unseen by those without grace.
structure_note: Verses 1792 to 1797 set the Lord beyond knowing; 1798 to 1804 sing grace as bond, release and indwelling, with the refrain அருள் and அகம்புகுந்தான்; 1805 to 1813 turn to cosmology: grace as the five acts, the nine forms (1807, 1810), and bindu ripening into maya and the worlds (1812, 1813).

1792.reading: The two states are night and day, form is soul and body, grace is virtue and austerity, and what stands within matching them is enjoyment.
1792.nuance: The verse is a list of pairs and its key words are unclear: இருபதம் may be 'two states' or 'two feet', and பொருவது may mean 'what matches' or 'what contends'. Read as a whole it seems to set grace among the pairs that shape embodied life, but I can't fix the last line.

1793.reading: Nandi is hard to see and beyond thought, and appears far off to those who would touch or approach him; but when the heart lies longing and gathered there, as the light of a lamp, the darkness ends.
1793.nuance: விளக்கொளி யான்நெஞ்சம் can be split as 'my heart, a lamp's light' or read with விளக்கொளியான் as the Lord who is the lamp's light, coming into the heart. Either way the darkness ends inside, not by reaching out.

1794.reading: Within the inner intent the world appears; if the darkness of aversion goes, the Lord stands there; if one searches the gathered mind steadily, one gains a knowing vision and becomes like the immortals.
1794.nuance: குறிப்பு (sign, intent, focus) and விகிர்தன் (the one who is other, a name of Siva) carry the verse. குறிப்பு may be the meditator's point of focus or the Lord's own will; the world 'appearing' in it is open to both.

1795.reading: Ages went by in not discerning; our Lord Pinnakan knows apart from us, and as the one who knows that knowledge is the companion of those who know fully, he draws near and knows, master of great nature.
1795.nuance: The play on அறி (know) runs through every line. Who knows what is hard to fix in lines 2 to 4; the plain point is that our ages of not knowing are met by a Lord who knows and comes near.

1796.reading: Once the deeds that run of themselves are destroyed, I no longer know; perhaps Nandi knows. When the flesh melts and one perceives awareness itself, our Lord of the gods is like honey.
1796.nuance: நானே அறிகிலன் may be humility or the claim that the 'I' as knower is gone once karma ends. ஊனே உருகி, the flesh melting, is the devotional image of the melting body found across Saiva hymns.

1797.reading: The Lord does not exist because I know him; those who knew the heavens were bewildered and did not know him; if the bright flame that knows the flesh and breathes within does not know him, who else will?
1797.nuance: The flame within (ஒண்சுடர்) may be the soul or the Lord himself. On the first reading only the soul's inner light can know him; on the second, only he knows himself.

1798.reading: People do not know how far grace reaches everywhere, do not discern that grace is nectar to be enjoyed, do not consider grace's great subtlety in the five acts; who knows that grace is the eye everywhere?
1798.nuance: Each line opens with அருள். The five acts (ஐங்கருமம்) are named here as grace's work, not only as power, which the chapter goes on to say outright (1805, 1809).

1799.reading: He grants knowledge so that the soul may draw near by knowing, lets desire in through the senses and joins with it, turns it into knowledge and gives the grace of his feet; those who stood close to him became Siva.
1799.nuance: அணு (the atom) is a Siddhanta name for the bound soul. The verse seems to say that even desire through the senses is used by grace, but who 'joins' (புணர்ந்திட்டு) is unclear.

1800.reading: Born in grace, grown in grace, wearing out, resting and vanishing in grace, fed the full nectar of bliss that is grace, by grace my Nandi entered my heart.
1800.nuance: The whole course of a life, birth, growth, decay, rest and disappearance, is set inside grace. இளைப்பாறி (resting) may point to the rest the soul has in dissolution before the next creation.

1801.reading: By grace he bathed me in the great sea of nectar, by grace joined me to his feet and gave me longing, fed me the full nectar of bliss that is grace, and by grace my Nandi entered there.
1801.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 nearly repeat 1800. அடிபுணைந்து can be 'joined to his feet' or 'his feet became my raft' (புணை), which suits the sea of line 1.

1802.reading: It was grace that put the soul into bonds, grace that let go its love of those bonds, grace that gives release without shame in that love, and grace is the state that does not appear in the love of that union.
1802.nuance: The striking claim is that binding too is grace. Siddhanta tradition reads it so: the soul is joined to bonds so that its root impurity may ripen and fall. Line 4 is compressed and I can't fix it.

1803.reading: The great gracious one who gave the way of no birth, the great ascetic Nandi who gave grace that does not forget, the Brahmin who is a sea of virtue, the first Supreme, came as kin and entered my heart.
1803.nuance: அறவாழி அந்தணன் is the Kural's own phrase for the Lord (Kural 8). மாதவன் here is 'great ascetic', not Vishnu. Nandi in Tirumular is both the Lord and the first guru, so the verse may also speak of the teacher.

1804.reading: By grace he entered the heart of me, his servant; though within, he is not seen by those without grace; entering, making bliss and becoming Siva, Nandi entered as the blissful one.
1804.nuance: அகம்புகுந்தான் opens every line, carried over from the end of 1800. Line 2 says the same indwelling Lord is in everyone but is not perceived without grace.

1805.reading: Great maya, which does not know, with the knowing soul; the instruments it makes, the five elements and the many senses with them: all these are the fivefold work of grace.
1805.nuance: ஆயும் அறிவோடு அறியாத மாமாயை is taken here as the soul (which knows) beside maya (which does not), the sentient and insentient. Calling the whole apparatus of body and senses grace's work follows 1802.

1806.reading: Grace is all the elemental world, grace is the Pure one become the moving and unmoving; the Lord who is called darkness and open space, everywhere, is grace, and there is none apart from embodied form.
1806.nuance: சகளம் is the Lord's form with parts, as against the formless. Line 4 (அருளே சகளத்தின் அன்றிஇன் றாமே) is unclear: it may mean grace is known only through form, or that nothing exists apart from it.

1807.reading: Siva with Shakti, shining nada, bindu, the five-faced Sadasiva of austerity, Isa, Hara, Mal who enters births and the lotus-born at the end: he dances, having become these nine.
1807.nuance: These are the nine forms (நவந்தரு பேதம்) of Siva in Siddhanta. Placing Vishnu (மால்) and Brahma among Siva's own forms ranks them under him. பவமுறும், 'who meets birth', may refer to Vishnu's avatars.

1808.reading: To those without the eye of grace the rare thing does not appear; to those with it Hara appears before them. To the dark-eyed even the sun does not appear; to the clear-eyed it is glorious light everywhere.
1808.nuance: The sun is visible to all but the blind; so the Lord is present to all but seen only with grace's eye. The fault lies in the seer, not in the light.

1809.reading: He himself creates, protects, destroys and conceals; doing these he himself grants release; he himself pervades and is the head.
1809.nuance: The five acts, with release (முத்தி) taking the place of the fifth, grace. தானே (he himself) opens every line: no other agent is involved.

1810.reading: The upper four are his formless forms; Sadasiva, unwavering, is form and formless; the lower four are lasting forms; the Lord, beyond measure, is all of them and yet one.
1810.nuance: This sorts the nine of 1807: Siva, Shakti, nada and bindu formless; Sadasiva both; Maheswara, Rudra, Vishnu and Brahma with form. துலையா (unweighable, or unfailing) and the last phrase அல்லது ஒன்றே are not fully clear.

1811.reading: Being one, he is the imperishable; standing as if he were the soul, he is the life of life; pressing close, he is also not those things, as a companion; his play stands in me as love.
1811.nuance: The verse seems to state the Siddhanta relation of Lord and soul: one with it, other than it, and with it as companion. The syntax is compressed and the reading is tentative.

1812.reading: The Spotless one, standing in love with Shakti, reaching kutila and nada, joining to become many kalas, ripens as a bindu that cannot be lost.
1812.nuance: குடிலை (kutila, the curved power), நாதம் and கலை are technical terms of the cosmology chapter 140 develops. வீயத்தகா, 'not fit to perish', may describe bindu as imperishable or as not to be spent.

1813.reading: The supreme bindu that ripens is itself all-pervading; from it ripen pure maya and the vast great maya, the branch of the gods, the rising mantras and Veda, and countless crores of worlds.
1813.nuance: தனிமாயை may be சுத்தமாயை (pure maya) and மாமாயை the great maya, the two levels of maya in Siddhanta; மனு here is mantra. The chain (1812 to 1813) links back to grace: what grace places is the whole cosmos.

links.note: Both name the Lord அறவாழி அந்தணன். In the Kural only those who reach his feet cross the other seas; in Tirumular he himself gives the way of no birth and comes into the heart as kin.
Both give the Lord the five acts. 1927 says it of the Supreme as seed and root of cause and effect; 1809 says it with தானே in every line, adding that he also grants release.
1807 lists the nine forms he dances as; 1810 sorts them into four formless, Sadasiva as form-formless, and four with form, while keeping him one.
Both make bindu the source that becomes Mahamaya and all the worlds; 1813 adds the gods, mantras and Veda to what ripens from it.

1792 says அருளது ஆவது அறமும் தவமும், what grace is, is virtue and austerity. 258 says the two ways that end weariness are தவம் and அறம், which the Lord of unfailing renown makes fruitful (விளைக்கும்). Both place virtue and austerity inside the Lord's grace rather than as the soul's own achievement.

1793 says Nandi is hard to see (காண்டற்கு அரியன்) and far off to those who would touch or approach him (தீண்டற்கும் சார்தற்கும் சேயன்). Thiruppugazh 1050 opens with Murugan who cannot be touched or seen directly: தொட அடாது நேராக வடிவு காண வாராது. Both deny touch and sight as ways to the Lord; 1793 adds that the darkness ends when the heart lies longing within.

2581 says that unless the Knower dwelling there makes us know (அறிவான் இருந்தங்கு அறிவிக்கின் அல்லால்), we do not know what he knows. 1795 says ages went by in not discerning, and the Lord, who knows, comes near and knows (சார்ந்தறிவான்). Both deny that the soul knows on its own; 1795 adds the long time lost before he draws near.

1796 says that when ஊனே உருகி the flesh melts and one perceives awareness, the Lord is தேனே யனையன், like honey. 325 says in the samadhi where சித்தம் உருக்கி the mind melts and becomes Siva, one drinks the சுத்த மது, pure honey of Siva's bliss. Both join melting to honey as the taste of union.

1798 says people do not consider grace's subtlety in the five acts (அருள்ஐங் கருமத்து அதிசூக்கம்). 2062 says the insentient world is அத்தன் அருளின் விளையாட்டிடம் and that cleansing the soul of mala is the way of his ஐங்கருமம். Both make the five acts the work of grace rather than of bare power.

2016 asks what can be done with cows grazing in the field (கொல்லையின் மேயும் பசுக்கள்) unless they are led across the boundary and joined to the Lord's feet (இறைவன் அடிகூட்டி). 1799 says grace lets desire in through the senses (பொறிவழி யாசை), turns it into knowledge and gives அடியருள். 2016 states the need; 1799 describes how grace uses the senses themselves to lead the soul to the feet.

A near-repeat: lines 3 and 4 are almost the same, அருளான ஆனந்தத்து ஆரமுது ஊட்டி அருளால் என்நந்தி அகம் (அதும்) புகுந்தானே. 1800 sets birth, growth and decay inside grace; 1801 sets bathing in the sea of nectar and joining to the feet inside it. Each opens the same refrain with a different course of grace.

Kural 10 has a பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல், a great sea of births, which only those who reach the Lord's feet can swim. 1801 has the Lord bathe him in அமுதப் பெருங்கடல், a great sea of nectar, and join him to his feet (அடிபுணைந்து, which can also read as the feet becoming a raft, புணை). The same great sea and the same feet appear, but in Tirumular the sea is nectar to bathe in, not births to cross.

432 says the Lord who made birth for joy also shut it into the suffering of the bond (துன்பஞ்செய் பாசத் துயருள் அடைத்தனன்). 1802 calls that same act grace: பாசத்தில் இட்டது அருள், it was grace that put the soul into bonds, and grace that loosens love of them and gives release. 1802 gives the reason 432 leaves unsaid: binding too is the Lord's grace.

Both end in the same phrase, கூசற்ற முத்தி, release without shame. 1574 has the true guru gather the bonds, bind them and pluck them out (பாசத்தைக் கூட்டியே கட்டிப் பறித்திட்டு) and join one to that release; 1802 has grace put the soul into bonds and lead it to the same release. The pair shows the guru of 1574 doing what 1802 attributes to grace.

1805 says maya, the instruments (கரணம்), the five elements and the senses are all அருள் ஐந்துமாம் அருட்செய்கை, the fivefold work of grace. 2211 says the Lord fashioned the bonds, the thirty-six tattvas and set the instruments (கருவியும் வைத்தனன்) so that the malas may be cut. Both treat the whole bodily apparatus as given by the Lord for the soul's release.

1737 says Shakti and Siva fill all that is fixed and all that moves (தாபர சங்கமம்) and are the earth and the cosmos. 1806 says the same of grace: அருளே சகலமும் ஆய பவுதிகம், grace is all the elemental world, and அருளே சராசரம், grace is the moving and unmoving. Put together, they show the Shakti of 1737 renamed as grace in 1806.

Kural 393 says only the learned have eyes (கண்ணுடையர்); the unlearned have two sores on their face. 1808 says only those with அருட்கண் (the eye of grace) see Hara, as the dark-eyed (இருட்கண்ணினோர்) cannot see even the sun. Both say having eyes is not the same as seeing: in the Kural the missing eye is learning, in Tirumular it is grace.

1810 sorts the Lord's forms into formless, அருவுரு (Sadasiva) and form, and says the Lord is all of them and yet one. Thiruppugazh 1247 seeks a Lord whose form is அருவுரு ஒழிதரு, past both form and the formless, and beyond talk of அவன் இவள் அது. On the reading that 1810 makes the Lord these nine forms, 1247 adds the condition that he is not exhausted by them; 1810's last words (துலையா இறை ... ஒன்றே) leave room for this.

1811 says the Lord stands உயிர்க்குயிராய், as the life of life, both one with the soul and other than it. 2504 opens உயிர்க்குயிராகி ஒழிவற்று அழிவற்று and adds that without him anava does not leave. Both name the Lord the life of life; 2504 draws from it the soul's dependence for release.

1812 has the Spotless one with Shakti reach குடிலை and நாதம், join to become many கலை, and ripen as விந்து. 964 has நாதம் rise spiralling from விந்து and the mistress of bonds become sixteen கலை and the fifty-one letters. Both trace the same chain of bindu, nada and kala, in opposite directions.

source_issues: 1794 line 3: சிந்தையைக் சிக்கென should be சிந்தையைச் சிக்கென (sandhi misprint).
1801 line 3 (அருளானஆனந்தந்து) is a misprint for அருளான ஆனந்தத்து, as in 1800; line 4 அதும்புகுந் தானே is probably a misprint for அகம்புகுந் தானே.
1792 and 1806 line 4 are obscure and may be corrupt.
